Online Book Dataset Analysis Using Web Scraping¶

Website: Books to Scrape¶

Objective:
To collect book data from an online website using web scraping and analyze book prices, ratings, categories, and availability using Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA).

1. Business Problem¶

To analyze an online book dataset collected through web scraping to understand book categories, pricing, ratings, and availability, and identify meaningful patterns in the collected data.

2. Objectives¶

  • Collecting book information using web scraping.
  • Analyzing book prices and ratings.
  • Identifying book categories.
  • Understanding price variation across categories.
  • Analyzing book availability.
  • Identifying meaningful patterns in the dataset.
  • Visualizing the findings using charts.

for book in books:

    # Extract book title
    title = book.select_one("h3 a")["title"]

    # Extract book price
    price_text = book.select_one(".price_color").get_text(strip=True)
    price = float(price_text.replace("£", "").replace("Â", ""))

    # Extract book rating

    rating_word = next(
        word for word in rating_classes
        if word in rating_map
    )
    rating = rating_map[rating_word]

    # Extract availability

        ".availability"
    ).get_text(" ", strip=True)

        else "Out of stock"
    )

    # Extract product URL

    product_url = urljoin(page_url, title_link["href"])

    # Store the extracted details
    books_data.append({
        "Title": title,
        "Price": price,
        "Rating": rating,
        "Availability": availability,
        "Product_URL": product_url
    })

# Step 6: Scrape 1000 Books from Books to Scrape

import requests
import pandas as pd
import time

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from urllib.parse import urljoin
from requests.exceptions import RequestException

# Website setup
base_url = "https://books.toscrape.com/"

headers = {
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
}

# Create a session
session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update(headers)

# Start with an empty list
books_data = []

# Convert text ratings into numbers
rating_map = {
    "One": 1,
    "Two": 2,
    "Three": 3,
    "Four": 4,
    "Five": 5
}


# Function to fetch a webpage with retries
def get_soup(url, retries=3):

    for attempt in range(retries):
        try:
            response = session.get(url, timeout=30)
            response.raise_for_status()

            return BeautifulSoup(
                response.text,
                "html.parser"
            )

        except RequestException as error:
            print(
                f"Request failed (attempt {attempt + 1}/{retries})"
            )

            if attempt < retries - 1:
                time.sleep(3)
            else:
                print("Could not access:", url)
                print("Error:", error)

    return None


# Visit all 50 listing pages
for page_num in range(1, 51):

    page_url = urljoin(
        base_url,
        f"catalogue/page-{page_num}.html"
    )

    print(f"\nScraping listing page {page_num}/50...")

    soup = get_soup(page_url)

    if soup is None:
        print("Skipping listing page:", page_num)
        continue

    books = soup.select("article.product_pod")

    # Extract details for every book on this page
    for book in books:

        try:
            # 1. Book title
            title_link = book.select_one("h3 a")
            title = title_link["title"]

            # 2. Book price
            price_text = book.select_one(
                ".price_color"
            ).get_text(strip=True)

            price = float(
                price_text.replace("£", "").replace("Â", "")
            )

            # 3. Book rating
            rating_classes = book.select_one(
                ".star-rating"
            )["class"]

            rating_word = next(
                word for word in rating_classes
                if word in rating_map
            )

            rating = rating_map[rating_word]

            # 4. Availability
            availability_text = book.select_one(
                ".availability"
            ).get_text(" ", strip=True)

            availability = (
                "In stock"
                if "In stock" in availability_text
                else "Out of stock"
            )

            # 5. Individual book URL
            product_url = urljoin(
                page_url,
                title_link["href"]
            )

            # 6. Book category
            product_soup = get_soup(product_url)

            if product_soup is not None:

                breadcrumb_links = product_soup.select(
                    "ul.breadcrumb li a"
                )

                category = (
                    breadcrumb_links[-1].get_text(strip=True)
                    if len(breadcrumb_links) >= 3
                    else None
                )

            else:
                category = None

            # Store the book details
            books_data.append({
                "Title": title,
                "Price": price,
                "Rating": rating,
                "Availability": availability,
                "Category": category,
                "Product_URL": product_url
            })

            # Brief pause between requests
            time.sleep(0.2)

        except (AttributeError, KeyError, ValueError, StopIteration) as error:
            print("Could not extract a book:", error)

    print("Records collected so far:", len(books_data))


# Create the final dataset
df = pd.DataFrame(books_data)

# Display the results
print("\n========== SCRAPING COMPLETED ==========")
print("Total records collected:", len(df))
print("Dataset shape:", df.shape)

print("\nDuplicate rows:", df.duplicated().sum())

print("\nMissing values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())

print("\nFirst 5 records:")
display(df.head())

# Step 7: Data Cleaning and Preparation

# 1. Create a copy of the original dataset
df_clean = df.copy()

# 2. Remove duplicate records
df_clean = df_clean.drop_duplicates()

# 3. Remove records without essential information
df_clean = df_clean.dropna(
    subset=["Title", "Price", "Rating", "Availability", "Category"]
)

# 4. Check and correct data types
df_clean["Title"] = df_clean["Title"].astype(str)
df_clean["Price"] = pd.to_numeric(
    df_clean["Price"], errors="coerce"
)
df_clean["Rating"] = pd.to_numeric(
    df_clean["Rating"], errors="coerce"
)

# 5. Remove records with invalid prices or ratings
df_clean = df_clean.dropna(
    subset=["Price", "Rating"]
)

df_clean = df_clean[
    (df_clean["Price"] >= 0) &
    (df_clean["Rating"].between(1, 5))
]

# 6. Reset the row index
df_clean = df_clean.reset_index(drop=True)

print("DATA CLEANING COMPLETED")
print("Original records:", len(df))
print("Records after cleaning:", len(df_clean))
print("Dataset shape:", df_clean.shape)

print("\nMissing values after cleaning:")
print(df_clean.isnull().sum())

print("\nDuplicate rows after cleaning:", df_clean.duplicated().sum())

display(df_clean.head())

# Step 11.2: Multivariate Analysis - Heatmap

# Calculate average price for each category and rating
heatmap_data = df_clean.pivot_table(
    index="Category",
    columns="Rating",
    values="Price",
    aggfunc="mean"
)

# Create the heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

sns.heatmap(
    heatmap_data,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".2f",
    cmap="YlGnBu",
    linewidths=0.5,
    cbar_kws={"label": "Average Price (£)"}
)

plt.title("Average Book Price by Category and Rating")
plt.xlabel("Book Rating (Stars)")
plt.ylabel("Book Category")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

extracting the books from each page¶

In [144]:
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from IPython.display import display, HTML
from urllib.parse import urljoin

base_url = "https://books.toscrape.com/"

for page_num in range(1, 6):

    page_url = urljoin(
        base_url,
        f"catalogue/page-{page_num}.html"
    )

    response = requests.get(page_url, timeout=20)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")

    print(f"PAGE {page_num}")
    print("-" * 50)

    books = soup.select("article.product_pod")

    for book in books:
        title = book.select_one("h3 a")["title"]
        price = book.select_one(".price_color").get_text(strip=True)

        print(f"Title: {title} | Price: {price}")

    print(f"Total books on Page {page_num}: {len(books)}")
    print("\n")

Chi-Square Test¶

In [136]:
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

# Create contingency table
contingency_table = pd.crosstab(df["Category"], df["Availability"])

print("Contingency Table:")
display(contingency_table)

# Chi-Square Test
chi2, p_value, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(contingency_table)

print("Chi-Square Statistic:", chi2)
print("P-Value:", p_value)
print("Degrees of Freedom:", dof)

# Interpretation
if p_value < 0.05:
    print("Result: Reject the Null Hypothesis")
    print("Conclusion: Category and Availability are significantly related.")
else:
    print("Result: Fail to Reject the Null Hypothesis")
    print("Conclusion: Category and Availability are not significantly related.")

One-Way ANOVA¶

In [137]:
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Create price groups for each category
groups = [group["Price"].values for name, group in df.groupby("Category")]

# Perform One-Way ANOVA
f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*groups)

print("F-Statistic:", f_statistic)
print("P-Value:", p_value)

if p_value < 0.05:
    print("Result: Reject the Null Hypothesis")
    print("Conclusion: Average book prices differ significantly across categories.")
else:
    print("Result: Fail to Reject the Null Hypothesis")
    print("Conclusion: No significant difference in average book prices across categories.")

F-Statistic: 0.6802439212356584
P-Value: 0.8713301337975456
